sentence: I have never been to London
explanation: 'Never' va entre 'have' y el participio pasado: 'have never been'.

sentence: She has already finished her homework
hint: 'Already' goes between has/have and the past participle
explanation: Con 'she' se usa 'has' (no 'have'). 'Already' va antes del participio pasado.

sentence: Have you ever visited Paris
hint: Questions: Have/Has + subject + ever + past participle
explanation: Preguntas en presente perfecto: Have + sujeto + ever + participio pasado.

sentence: They have just arrived at the hotel
explanation: 'Just' va entre 'have' y el participio pasado para acciones recientes.

sentence: He has not eaten anything today
explanation: Con 'he' se usa 'has not' (no 'have not'). 'Eat' → 'eaten' (irregular).

sentence: We have lived here for five years
hint: 'For' is used with periods of time
explanation: 'For' + período de tiempo: 'for five years'. Se coloca al final.

sentence: Has she ever tried Japanese food
explanation: Con 'she' se usa 'Has' (no 'Have') en las preguntas.

sentence: I have already seen that movie twice
explanation: 'Already' va entre have y el participio pasado. 'Twice' va al final.

sentence: They have not finished the project yet
hint: 'Yet' goes at the end in negatives
explanation: 'Yet' va al final de las oraciones negativas: 'have not finished...yet'.

sentence: She has worked here since January
hint: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time
explanation: 'Since' + momento específico: 'since January'. Se usa 'has' con 'she', no 'have'.

sentence: Have they ever been to a concert
explanation: Pregunta: Have + sujeto + ever + participio pasado.

sentence: He has just left the office
explanation: Con 'he' se usa 'has'. 'Just' se usa para acciones muy recientes: 'has just left'.

sentence: I have not spoken to her recently
explanation: 'Speak' → 'spoken' (irregular). 'Recently' va al final.

sentence: We have known each other for ten years
explanation: 'Know' → 'known' (irregular). 'For' + duración va al final.

sentence: Has he already read the new book
explanation: Con 'he' se usa 'Has' en las preguntas. 'Already' va antes del participio pasado.

sentence: She has never forgotten her first day at school
explanation: 'Forget' → 'forgotten'. 'Never' va entre has y el participio pasado.

sentence: I have always wanted to learn French
explanation: 'Always' va entre have y el participio pasado: 'have always wanted'.

sentence: They have not decided where to go yet
explanation: El negativo + 'yet' va al final. 'Where to go' es una pregunta incrustada (embedded question).

sentence: He has traveled to many countries
explanation: Con 'he' se usa 'has', no 'have'.

sentence: Have you finished your dinner yet
explanation: 'Yet' va al final de las preguntas: 'Have you finished...yet?'
